sections.title: Moss mat
sections.text: Rhytidiadelphus squarrosus, springy turf-moss, is a robust pleurocarpous moss that forms loose, spreading mats or lawns in grassland and other open habitats. Individual shoots may reach about 15 cm.

sections.title: Identification
sections.text: Its pale-green shoots have reddish stems and conspicuous leaves bent sharply outward, giving each shoot a starry look from above. Mosses have no true roots, flowers or seeds; sporophytes, when present, produce spores in capsules.

sections.title: Plate comparison
sections.text: The illustration shows the loose tuft and sharply spreading leaves typical of this moss. Its enlarged capsule is a representative moss sporophyte; capsule production is not always visible in field populations.
